title: Bible Parable: A Helpful Samaritan
description: An injured traveler receives practical help on the road. Optional Bible interest: Luke 10:25–37.
cardDescription: An injured traveler receives practical help on the road. Optional Bible interest: Luke 10:25–37.
focus: Story setting: Luke 10:25–37. Read the names as part of this particular story, rather than a chapter-and-verse quiz.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Helpful traveler in Jesus' neighbor parable
Cooking fat that is liquid at room temperature
Strip of cloth covering an injury
Creature on which the injured traveler was carried

answerNotes.ROAD: A road is a route for vehicles. A sidewalk or footpath provides a different part of the journey for people on foot.
answerNotes.OIL: Oil has different uses in different scenes. It can be a cooking ingredient, lamp fuel, or part of a story about caring for a traveler.
answerNotes.COIN: A coin is a metal piece of money. The value depends on the currency and period; Bible stories do not use modern U.S. coins.
answerNotes.SAMARITAN: Helpful traveler in Jesus' neighbor parable. This scene follows Luke 10:25–37; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.NEIGHBOR: Person living nearby. This scene follows Luke 10:25–37; the passage gives the story's context.

cardDescription: A shepherd's call and a flock illustrate a familiar teaching. Optional Bible interest: John 10:1–18.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Farm animal known for its woolly fleece
Go behind someone along the same path
Be familiar with someone or something
Say a name to get attention
Grass-covered land where ranch livestock graze
Looking after another person or animal

answerNotes.SHEPHERD: Person caring for sheep. This scene follows John 10:1–18; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.VOICE: Sound made when speaking. This scene follows John 10:1–18; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.SHEEP: Sheep are farm animals valued for wool and other products. A lamb is a young sheep, and an ewe is an adult female.
answerNotes.GATE: A gate opens through a fence or other boundary. Hinges let it move, and a latch holds it closed.
answerNotes.CALL: Call can mean telephone contact or saying a name aloud. Both uses involve trying to get someone's attention.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.

title: Bible Parable: A House Built on Rock
subtheme: Bible Parable: A House Built on Rock
description: Two building sites show what happens when rain and flood arrive. Optional Bible interest: Matthew 7:24–27.
cardDescription: Two building sites show what happens when rain and flood arrive. Optional Bible interest: Matthew 7:24–27.
focus: Story setting: Matthew 7:24–27. Read the names as part of this particular story, rather than a chapter-and-verse quiz.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Fine loose grains on a beach
Put parts together to make a structure
Water spreading over normally dry land
Support that holds an object upright
Weather with strong wind and rain

answerNotes.ROCK: Hard piece of natural stone. This scene follows Matthew 7:24–27; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.HOUSE: Building used as a dwelling. This scene follows Matthew 7:24–27; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.SAND: Sand consists of small loose grains. A pebble is much larger than an individual grain of sand.
answerNotes.RAIN: Rain is liquid water falling from clouds. Snow and hail reach the ground in solid forms instead.
answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.

answerNotes.LAMP: Oil-burning light in a Bible teaching. This scene follows Matthew 5:14–16; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.HOUSE: A house is a building. Home is the place associated with living and belonging, which need not be a separate house.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.STAND: Base on which an object rests. This scene follows Matthew 5:14–16; the passage gives the story's context.
